title: [Discordant autoimmune heart block in twins: a case report and literature review].
abstract: Congenital atrioventricular block (AVB) is a cardiac conduction disorder that may occur as a manifestation of neonatal lupus. The most common etiology is autoimmune and is mediated by maternal anti-SSA (Ro) and anti-SSB (La) antibodies; however, their presence alone is insufficient to induce the disease, suggesting the involvement of additional genetic or environmental factors. We report the case of a dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy with maternal autoimmunity, in which only one of the fetuses developed complete AVB. Management included hydroxychloroquine therapy, resulting in fetal hemodynamic stability and the absence of major complications during gestation. After birth, the affected neonate required permanent pacemaker implantation with a favorable clinical outcome. In addition, a narrative review of the literature was conducted addressing the pathophysiological mechanisms, prenatal screening, and therapeutic strategies for autoimmune AVB, reinforcing the prophylactic role of hydroxychloroquine and the importance of close surveillance. This case illustrates the potential influence of additional fetal factors on susceptibility to cardiac injury and highlights the need to continue reporting these infrequent presentations in order to optimize diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Severe Organ Involvement in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Retrospective Single-Center Study From Morocco.
abstract: Introduction Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by multisystem inflammatory involvement and an unpredictable clinical course. SLE is among the most prevalent autoimmune diseases in Morocco, yet epidemiological and clinical data from this region remain limited. Disease management relies mainly on conventional therapies, with restricted access to advanced targeted treatments. Objective To describe the epidemiological, clinical, biological, and therapeutic characteristics of patients diagnosed with SLE in an internal medicine department in Morocco, with a particular focus on severe renal, hematological, and neurological manifestations. Methods We conducted a retrospective descriptive study including 61 patients diagnosed with SLE between January 2017 and September 2022 at the Internal Medicine Department of the International University Hospital Cheikh Khalifa Ibn Zaid in Casablanca, Morocco. Diagnosis was established according to the 2019 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology (EULAR/ACR) and/or the 2012 Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics (SLICC) classification criteria. Data were collected from medical records and analyzed using descriptive statistical methods. Results The study population was predominantly female (n=55; 90.2%), with a mean age at diagnosis of 40.3 years (SD 14.2; median 40; range 13-74). The most common manifestations were fatigue (82.0%), arthralgia (70.5%), and malar rash (59.0%). Hematological involvement was prominent: anemia was present in 29 patients (47.5%), of whom 10 (16.4%) had confirmed autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA). Renal involvement was identified in 10 patients (16.4%); among the seven who underwent biopsy, class IV lupus nephritis predominated (n=5; 71.4%). Neurological involvement was documented in 14 patients (22.5%), with the majority comprising nonfocal manifestations such as persistent headaches and mood disorders. Most patients were treated with hydroxychloroquine (n=48; 78.7%) and systemic corticosteroids (n=38; 62.3%); immunomodulatory therapy was required in 18 patients (29.5%). Of the 39 patients with complete follow-up (median 28 months), 14 (35.9%) achieved complete remission, 19 (48.7%) achieved partial remission, 13 (33.3%) experienced disease relapse, and six (15.4%) achieved neither. Conclusion This single-center Moroccan cohort highlights a substantial burden of hematological involvement and reveals a treatment landscape defined by restricted access to biologic therapies. The findings underscore the need for region-specific epidemiological data, improved access to targeted treatments, and dedicated prospective research to better characterize SLE in North African populations.

title: Hydroxychloroquine-induced cytotoxicity in ARPE-19 cells involves PI3K/AKT-associated signaling: network toxicology and functional validation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is widely used for the long-term treatment of autoimmune and rheumatologic disorders, but retinal toxicity remains an important adverse effect. Although lysosomal and autophagic dysfunction have been implicated in HCQ-associated retinal injury, the signaling networks involved in the cellular response to HCQ remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the potential involvement of PI3K/AKT-associated signaling in HCQ-induced cytotoxicity.
METHODS: Network toxicology and molecular docking were integrated to identify candidate HCQ-associated targets, followed by experimental validation in human retinal pigment epithelial ARPE-19 cells. Cell viability was evaluated by CCK-8 assay, and apoptosis was assessed by Annexin V/PI flow cytometry. The expression of predicted hub genes and proteins was examined by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. AKT phosphorylation was evaluated across HCQ concentration and time gradients. The AKT activator SC79 was further used in pharmacological rescue experiments to assess the functional involvement of AKT signaling in HCQ-induced apoptosis.
RESULTS: Network analysis identified PIK3CA, PIK3R1, SRC, JAK2, and PTPN11 as candidate hub proteins associated with PI3K/AKT-related signaling. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions between HCQ and these proteins, with variable docking energies among targets. HCQ reduced ARPE-19 cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner, with a 24-h IC50 of 59.51 μM, and increased apoptosis with increasing concentrations. qRT-PCR revealed concentration-dependent and gene-specific transcriptional responses rather than uniform suppression of all five hub genes, whereas Western blotting showed an overall reduction in the abundance of the candidate hub proteins after 24 h HCQ exposure. AKT phosphorylation exhibited dynamic regulation: short-term HCQ exposure increased p-AKT/AKT at higher concentrations, whereas an independent 30 μM time-course experiment showed an overall decline in AKT phosphorylation during prolonged exposure. Importantly, SC79 pretreatment enhanced p-AKT/AKT under HCQ exposure and partially attenuated HCQ-induced apoptosis.
CONCLUSION: These findings support the involvement of PI3K/AKT-associated signaling in HCQ-induced cytotoxicity in ARPE-19 cells. HCQ induces concentration- and time-dependent alterations in this signaling network, while pharmacological enhancement of AKT signaling partially reduces the apoptotic response. The results provide functional evidence that AKT signaling contributes to the cellular response to HCQ and support further investigation of PI3K/AKT-associated signaling in HCQ-related RPE injury.

title: Urolithin A ameliorates experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravisin association with mitochondrial quality control-related and inflammasome signaling changes.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) remodeling in myasthenia gravis (MG) at the pathway and transcriptomic level, and to evaluate whether urolithin A (UA) ameliorates experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravis (EAMG) in association with altered mitochondrial quality control-related and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.
METHODS: Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from two patients with stable MG and two with MC were analyzed. After quality control, 8414 stable-MG cells and 19,333 MC cells were retained. Cell composition, pathway scores, pseudobulk differential expression, gene-set enrichment, and ligand-receptor interactions were assessed. In parallel, EAMG rats were assigned to control, EAMG, EAMG+UA, or EAMG+UA + chloroquine groups (n = 6/group). Clinical, serological, inflammatory, ultrastructural, mitochondrial quality control-related, and inflammasome-related outcomes were evaluated.
RESULTS: MC samples showed heterogeneous immune remodeling, including monocyte enrichment in one patient. Across immune-cell subsets, MC was associated with increased inflammatory, inflammasome/pyroptosis, oxidative-stress, chemotaxis, and lysosome-autophagy programs, whereas mitochondrial quality control-related changes were weaker and cell-type dependent. Exploratory analysis suggested enhanced TNFSF13B-TNFRSF13C interaction scores toward B-cell subsets. In EAMG rats, UA reduced clinical weakness, anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and pro-inflammatory cytokines; improved splenic mitochondrial ultrastructure and PINK1/Parkin-associated mitochondrial quality control marker profiles; and suppressed NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD-N signaling. Chloroquine partially reversed these effects.
CONCLUSION: Exploratory scRNA-seq analysis of four patients suggests that MC is associated with pathway-level enrichment of inflammasome/pyroptosis and autophagy/lysosome programs, whereas mitochondrial quality control-related signals were weaker and cell-type-dependent. The EAMG findings support an association between UA treatment, improved mitochondrial quality control-related marker profiles, and reduced inflammasome activation.
